title: OpenShape 3D
say: Welcome to OpenShape 3D, a free, open-source CAD app for iPad. In this video we'll cover the basics of solid modeling, and then build a simple part from scratch, step by step.

title: What is CAD?
say: CAD stands for computer-aided design. Instead of pushing polygons around, a solid modeler works with exact geometry: flat faces, cylinders and precise dimensions. That's what lets you export a part for 3D printing or machining, and have it come out right.

title: The four steps
sub: How almost every part is built
say: Almost every part follows the same four steps. Sketch a two-D profile. Turn it into a solid. Refine it with tools like fillet and shell. And combine bodies with booleans. Let's look at a finished model first.

title: Sample designs
say: The app ships with sample designs. Tap Add Sample Designs, and they land in a Demos folder in your gallery. Let's open the motorcycle wheel.

title: Motorcycle Wheel
lines: Rim: a profile revolved around an axis
Orbit, pinch to zoom, standard views
say: Here's the motorcycle wheel. The rim is a profile revolved around an axis. The spoke holes are one cut, repeated in a circular pattern. And the tyre is a separate body. You can orbit with one finger, pinch to zoom, and jump to the standard views.

title: Parametric history
say: Everything you do is recorded as a feature in the History panel. Change a dimension in an early step, and the whole model rebuilds. That's parametric modeling.

title: Your first part
lines: Palette on the left: Sketch, Modify, Transform, Combine
say: Now let's build something. Go back and start a blank design. The tool palette is on the left: Sketch, Modify, Transform and Combine. The viewport in the middle shows your model, and the toolbar on top has the views, undo, and the Items and History panels.

title: Step 1 · Sketch
lines: Draw, then type the exact size
say: Step one: sketch. Pick the Sketch tool and the Rectangle. Tap the ground plane and draw a rectangle. Then type the exact size: forty by twenty-four millimeters.

title: Step 2 · Holes
say: Add two circles for the mounting holes, six millimeters across, centered twelve millimeters either side of the middle. Dimensions you type are constraints: they hold when you edit the sketch later.

title: Step 3 · Extrude
say: Step two: make it solid. Select the profile and choose Extrude. Pull it up, or type a distance: six millimeters. Notice the circles became holes. A closed loop inside another loop is cut out automatically.

title: Step 4 · Fillet
say: Step three: refine. Tap Modify, then Fillet, and tap the four vertical corner edges. A four millimeter radius rounds them off.

title: Step 5 · Fillet
lines: Same tool, the top edge loop
A small radius softens the part
say: Do the same on the top edges with a one millimeter radius, to soften the part.

title: Step 6 · Boss
sub: Sketch on a face, extrude with Union
lines: Sketch a circle on the top face
Union fuses it into one solid
say: Now add a boss. Sketch a circle on the top face, and extrude it four and a half millimeters with the Union option, so it fuses into the plate as one solid. That's a boolean.

title: Step 7 · Appearance
lines: Looks only: the geometry stays exact
say: Give it a material from the body menu. This is only for looks. The geometry underneath stays exact. Then check it from the front, the top, and the isometric view.

title: Undo and redo
lines: Or edit the step in History
say: Made a mistake? Undo and redo work for every step. Or open History and edit the step directly.

title: Export and share
say: When you're done, export STEP, STL, 3MF, OBJ or DXF from the share menu. No account, no cloud. OpenShape 3D is open source on GitHub. Thanks for watching, and happy modeling.
